title: Gale demo: Mount Sharp corridor survey and replanning
summary: The drone surveys an uncertain corridor, finds a scarp, the first route is invalidated and the astronaut is replanned around it, reaches goal B and returns to base.
disclaimer: Terrain: NASA/USGS MSL Gale crater DEM mosaic crop over Curiosity's traverse and the foot of Mount Sharp (real, provisional, 8 m display grid from its 8 m overview). Rover stop markers: real Curiosity stops (NASA). Mission, budgets and the corridor scarp are simulated or synthetic; POIs C and D are real Curiosity science sites (NASA), visited here in a simulated story. Rover (1 m/s) and drone (4 m/s, 40 m up) motion is simulated; the rover is faster than real hardware (Perseverance about 4.2 cm/s), the drone below the Ingenuity top speed (about 5 m/s, flown at 10-24 m). Not EVA-certified limits, not a planner output.

ai_disclosure.scope: Fixture generator script and replay fixture structure; the simulated mission, routes and events are generated data, not observations.
ai_disclosure.observational_data: Only the terrain heights come from NASA/USGS data; everything else here is simulated.

imagery.title: MRO CTX Gale crater mosaic (block adjusted)

imagery.processing: Bilinear resampling onto the crop ENU grid; display contrast stretched linearly between the 1st and 99th percentile. Panchromatic; the viewer tints it for display only.

terrain_meta.crs: Local tangent ENU grid; source Equirectangular, Mars 2000 sphere IAU (R = 3396190 m)
terrain_meta.vertical_datum: Mars datum of the MSL Gale DEM mosaic; local z = elevation - (-4162 m)
sources: MSL Gale crater DEM mosaic, 1 m, v3 (MRO HiRISE and CTX stereo), USGS Astrogeology Science Center / NASA. File MSL_Gale_DEM_Mosaic_1m_v3.tif (overview level 1, 8 m per pixel, in MSL_Gale_DEM_Mosaic_1m_v3.tif.ovr), MD5 of the full file as published bc4cbabf8b06d24f3b25400f0468933b.
Product page https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/mars_msl_gale_merged_dem_mosaic. Native resolution 8 m. Not verified here: USGS-hosted NASA planetary data, see the product page for usage terms.

Crop: 950 x 425 cells of 8 m centred at -4.7253 N, 137.3865 E, bicubic (Catmull-Rom) resampling of the 8 m overview onto a local tangent ENU grid (east = R cos(lat) dlon, north = R dlat); 8 m cells, so no resolution gain. PROVISIONAL, made by the frontend until the data owner delivers the processed package.
SYNTHETIC: a scarp was added to the hidden evaluator reference to create an adverse case. It does not exist in the NASA terrain data.
ILLUSTRATIVE: uncertainty (sigma), budgets, speeds and consumption rates are assumptions of a simulated mission.

source.text: Real Curiosity stop 45_996, sol 940 (Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity waypoints (MMGIS MSL)); the base sits on the nearest walkable cell, within 12 m.
Real Curiosity stop 53_1990, sol 1284 (Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity waypoints (MMGIS MSL)); the goal sits on the nearest walkable cell, within 12 m.

Real Curiosity science site: Buckskin, drill hole, sol 1060. Placed at the rover's published position at the time (stop 48_2542), on the nearest drivable cell within 12 m. Source: NASA/JPL PIA21254, Curiosity's Rock or Soil Sampling Sites on Mars, Through November 2016 (drill holes).

Real Curiosity science site: Big Sky, drill hole, sol 1119. Placed at the rover's published position at the time (stop 50_592), on the nearest drivable cell within 12 m. Source: NASA/JPL PIA21254, Curiosity's Rock or Soil Sampling Sites on Mars, Through November 2016 (drill holes).

Real Curiosity science site nearest to goal B that the astronaut can walk to: Lubango, drill hole, sol 1320, at the rover's published position (stop 54_746). 0.11 km on foot from goal B (project slope limit 20 degrees). Source: NASA/JPL PIA21254, Curiosity's Rock or Soil Sampling Sites on Mars, Through November 2016 (drill holes).

Chosen by the demo generator with a published NASA criterion, not a NASA site: the 1 km x 1 km area with the gentlest ground of the NASA DEM that meets the civil-engineering slope criterion of NASA's 2015 human Exploration Zone rubric (slope under 10 degrees at the 1 km scale: 4.2 degrees; within 5 km of the landing site, here base A: 2.61 km). Mean 8 m slope 4.9 degrees, 3 % of cells above 10 degrees. The rubric's ~50 km2 area and sparse rocks are not checked (crop too small, no rock-abundance data); water ice and hydrated minerals are not assessed here (see the water, ice and radiation section of docs/science_poi_dossier.md).
